'''V-slips''' (also '''Virtual slips''') are printable overlays released by the [[Players Committee]] so players can use Virtual card text on physical Decipher ''Star Wars'' CCG cards. Early instructions told players to print the PDF, cut out the new game text, and insert it in an opaque sleeve with the matching Decipher card. With clear sleeves, players taped or attached the cutout to the card.<ref name="tfn2002">[https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Player's Committee Announces the First Virtual Card Set], TheForce.Net, 12 February 2002 (citing Game Players Network)</ref><ref name="decivs1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020610072829if_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee/virtualcardset1.html Virtual Card Set #1 is Away!], decipher.com (Wayback, 10 June 2002 snapshot; dated 5 March 2002)</ref><ref name="vc1pdf">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050813215254/http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/virtual/VirtualCards1.pdf VirtualCards1.pdf], decipher.com (Wayback)</ref><ref name="cardlists">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611031545/http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Decipher Star Wars CCG cardlists index], decipher.com (Internet Archive, 11 June 2002)</ref>

Decipher's own June 2002 cardlists index listed Players Committee virtual sets next to official products and described printable PDF slips for tournament-legal play:<ref name="cardlists" />

<blockquote>In addition, virtual card sets from the SWCCG Player's Committee provide new game text for selected cards. In printable PDF format, text may be sleeved with your original cards for tournament-legal play.</blockquote>
<blockquote>Virtual Card Set #1 &ndash; 12 cards. Tournament-legal 03-09-02.</blockquote>

Official download and print libraries still live under [https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/virtual-slips/ Virtual Slips / Files] on starwarsccg.org.<ref name="slips">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/virtual-slips/ Virtual Slips / Files], starwarsccg.org</ref>

== How players use them ==

Per early Decipher / Players Committee material (2002):

* Virtual cards shipped as '''PDF slips''' &mdash; print, cut, sleeve over the referenced Decipher card.<ref name="tfn2002" /><ref name="decivs1" /><ref name="cardlists" />
* Virtual versions were marked with '''(V)''' in rulings, articles, and deck lists.<ref name="decivs1" />
* Players could include both the original Decipher text and the (V) version in a deck, but could not switch a card either way once a tournament began.<ref name="decivs1" />

Surviving early slip PDFs (e.g. VirtualCards1.pdf / VirtualCards1a.pdf) show compact replacement game-text boxes for specific Premiere cards.<ref name="vc1pdf" /><ref name="vc1apdf">[https://web.archive.org/web/20070117223920/http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/virtual/VirtualCards1a.pdf VirtualCards1a.pdf], decipher.com (Wayback)</ref> Later PC slips expanded beyond those compact modifiers.

Premium Virtual Set 1 slips work the same way: cut out the area beneath the card title and sleeve it with the original card. Opaque sleeves are recommended; clear sleeves may need tape.<ref name="vs1prem">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualCards1Premium.pdf VirtualCards1Premium.pdf], res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks &mdash; Virtual Set #1 Premium Edition</ref>

Later Players Committee slips are printable "new game text boxes (and sometimes new card names and frames)" placed over existing cards.<ref name="pcabout">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/about-us/ About Us], starwarsccg.org</ref><ref name="pcabout2">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/about/ About], starwarsccg.org</ref><ref name="pcabout3">[https://playerscommittee.org/about/ About], playerscommittee.org</ref>

== V-Kit ==

[https://www.starwarsccg.org/vkit/ Vkit] on starwarsccg.org (app at [https://vkit.starwarsccg.org/ vkit.starwarsccg.org]) is the Players Committee tool for generating customized printable Virtual-card PDFs (select cards / sets rather than only whole-set slip PDFs).<ref name="vkit">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/vkit/ Vkit], starwarsccg.org</ref><ref name="vkitapp">[https://vkit.starwarsccg.org/ V-Kit app], vkit.starwarsccg.org</ref><ref name="vkitgh">[https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-vkit swccgpc/swccg-vkit], GitHub</ref> The Virtual Slips library also points players to vKit for a custom selection of slips.<ref name="slips" />
